en: The *Sūtra of the Holy Invincible Vajra Fire Dhāraṇī*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Imperially Appointed Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Teaching, the Subject Fǎtián, in accordance with the Imperial Edict.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying within the Jewel-Peak Pavilion on Mount Sumeru,
which was adorned with various kinds of gold and jewels.
Countless rays of light issued forth, illuminating all the mountains and rocky crags on every side.
Furthermore, there were sandalwood, aloeswood, ointment incense, powdered incense, and various kinds of famous flowers,
as well as precious canopies and bells, thus adorning [the scene].
At that time, there were devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, as well as vidyādharas,
bhūtas, piśācas, vetālas, and hosts of mātṛs, both with form and without form.
The assembly gathered and sat down, filling an area of five hundred yojanas.
Furthermore, there were seven thousand five hundred bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and twelve thousand five hundred bhikṣus.
They all came together to the assembly to listen to the Dharma.
At that time, the assembly consisted of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, gandharvas, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
The hosts of vidyādharas, bhūtas, pināyakas, piśācas, and the mātṛkā spirits—
both those with form and those without form—
cried out in a loud voice, "Alas! Alas!"
Then the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni asked again:
"Why do you cry out in loud voices, saying 'We are terrified and afflicted by suffering'?
Those multitudes replied:
“World-Honored One, I have been terrified and subdued by a powerful holy being; I have now come here.
I pray only that you, out of compassion, will grant me special protection.
The World-Honored One replied:
Now, within this most supreme and vast maṇḍala,
there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have attained the stage of the great earth and are destined to succeed to the rank of the consecrated Dharma King.

Having spoken these words— "One who is able to awaken to the various karmas of good and evil shall bring comfort to your mind"— in that very instant, there appeared a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva named Vajrapāṇi.
Like a mountain of vajra, he emits golden light that universally illuminates the world.
He wears a jeweled crown upon his head, his face is like the full moon,
and in his hands he holds a vajra staff, a vajra kīla, and a vajra lasso.
Possessing great power of merit, he is able to destroy all evils.
He leads five thousand families of Vajras as his retinue;
their names are the Great General Vajra-nanda and others.
The General Vajravajraghara, the General Vajravajraketu, and the General Vajravajravāsa.
The Vajranīla-vajra General, the Vajraratna-vajra General, and the Vajrāṅkuśa-vajra General.
The Vajra-maker Kīlaravajra Mahāsenāpati, the Vajra Mahāvajrananda-nātha,
and the Vajra World-protecting Vidyārāja.
Furthermore, Vajramāra, Vajrapiṇāka, Vajratārakumāra, Vajroṣṭraka, Vajramahāghora,
and others all gathered together within the great maṇḍala.
He emitted pure light that illuminated everything,
causing the hearts of all sentient beings to be filled with joy.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi...
Baring his right shoulder, he prostrated at the Buddha’s feet,
circumambulated him three times to the right, and stood with palms joined. At that time,
the World-Honored One addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Now, within this assembly there are devas, nāgas, yakṣas, asuras, and various classes of bhūtas who cry out in loud voices, terrified and distressed.
You should comfort them and bring them joy.
Thereupon, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi rose from his seat and entered a samādhi before the assembly of bhūtas, including devas, nāgas, and asuras;
it was named "The Radiant Lamp of the Supreme Vajra Weapon."
He manifests great supernormal powers such that thunder, hail, lightning, and massive flames arise throughout the trichiliocosm.
When these sentient beings see this, their suffering, affliction,
and fear are immediately dispelled.
Furthermore, there were sentient beings as numerous as the sands of the Ganges who,
having witnessed this event, gave rise to a mind of pure brahmacarya, upholding the precepts and practicing patience,
and offered all their wealth and treasures to the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
All wished to follow and listen to the sublime Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi [addressed] the assembly of devas, nāgas, and yakṣas.
He taught the four truths, dependent origination, the gateways of samādhi, the ten pāramitās,
as well as the ritual procedures for the fundamental Vajra-family great maṇḍala.
All the Brahmā kings and the god Maheśvara...
Varuṇa, Kuśīra, Māruta, Āruṇa, Nārāyaṇa, Yāma, and Śakra.
As for those who attain accomplishment:
the asuras and gandharvas are those who attain accomplishment.
Even those such as the various evil bhūtas and mahārākṣasas who are difficult to subdue, he is able to subdue;
those who harbor malicious intent, he causes to give rise to a virtuous mind.
Those who harbor wrong views attain right view;
those who harbor malice give rise to loving-kindness and compassion;
and those who harbor ignorance and delusion become clearly enlightened.
Those who previously possessed great power lose that power;
those who were previously able to conceal their bodies can no longer do so;
and they are able to personally suppress and sever the mantras of others.
One should seek fulfillment through the mantras;
dwelling within the maṇḍala, one awakens and subdues [the afflictions].
It should be done in this manner.
At that time, the Buddha commanded Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva:
"You shall proclaim the Great Dharani of the Invincible Vajra Fire for them to receive and uphold.
Thus spoke Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva.
By the very power of the true majesty of this dhāraṇī,
it emits a great radiance that illuminates the entire assembly of worthy sages, including those gods, humans, asuras, and others.
Furthermore, by the power of the dhāraṇī,
the radiance of the sun, moon, and stars was made to disappear;
the great ocean surged and boiled, and Sumeru, the king of mountains, trembled in its entirety.
At that time, within the Golden Jewel Peak of the Great Radiant Flame Treasury,
there was a Vajrapāṇi maiden who transformed her own body into a great blazing flame and immediately ascended into the void.
He circumambulated the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta three times to the right, prostrated himself in homage,
and standing to one side, addressed that assembly, saying:
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva spoke the heart-mantra of the Tathāgata’s samādhi:
"You all should each cast aside your vajra weapons and the like,
and seek this great dhāraṇī method."
At that time, the World-Ruler Mahābrahmā, along with the devas, humans, asuras, and others,
all raised their voices and said:
"As the Bodhisattva has commanded, we shall now carry it out."
Thereupon, Maheśvara abandoned his trident;
Nārāyaṇa abandoned his wheel;
and Yāma abandoned his staff.
Kubera abandons his staff;
Śakra abandons his vajra; Māraṇa abandons his noose.
The celestial Māras relinquished their obstacles;
the asuras relinquished their power;
and the mārutās relinquished their delusive attachments.
The hosts of mātṛkā spirits were freed from distraction;
the hosts of nāgas and devas were freed from the poison of malice;
and the yakṣas, rākṣasas, kiṃnaras, piśācas, bhūtas, pretas, mahoragas, rākṣasīs, and kumbhāṇḍas—all had their power removed.
With single-minded reverence before the Bodhisattva,
Vajrapāṇi then spoke this dhāraṇī: *Namo ratnatrayāya namo śakrāya...*
Hana-vajra-praṇaye mahāyakṣasenāpate tadyathā tathāgatasamādhi-dhāraṇī-māvaliteśye.
Mimihe vāri-kūṭila-kūṭi-pāvaka-kula-śikhika-bhīra-ke śitaci-caci-juci-muṭṭha-nikka-rucici-vaci-vāriṇi-deyu-ruḷe.
Mumukhu mumukhu sumu sumu bharasara sphoṭa sphoṭa sphoṭa sphoṭa unneti piṅgale caṇḍi caṇḍi jvala piṅgale sarva...
Nivāgaṇapraharanamaya siddhaneji suṃdaru vajrakūṇi nṛtyasara praharaṇiratnatrāya ṇe.
*Kālabuti vajradhara viśvasani kṛtapramardani svāhā*. If there is anyone who hears this *dhāraṇī*, [they shall be protected].
If one recites, studies, recollects, and upholds this with single-minded devotion,
that person shall attain entry into the samādhi of all mundane and supramundane maṇḍalas. If anyone rejoices in it or pays it reverence, [they shall likewise attain such realization].
Such a person shall not be afflicted or harmed by prohibitions, mantras, various poisons, or any terrors.
At that time, the Buddha commanded the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi to proclaim the Great Dhāraṇī.
All the sons of the gods from the heavens of the desire and form realms rained down various exquisite and wonderful fragrant flowers from the midst of the sky as an offering,
and further praised him with sublime Brahma-sounds in song.
At that time, all the holy ones, bhikṣus, and the assembly of great bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the Great Maṇḍala gathering were filled with great joy;
they received it with faith and practiced accordingly.
The Sūtra of the Holy Invincible Vajra-fire Dhāraṇī.
